explanation:
[EFFECT] Wind speed has a near-neutral effect on predicted demand when winds are calm — at very low speeds (up to roughly 20 km/h, i.e. normalised values up to ~0.30), the model's contribution stays close to zero or marginally positive, with a slight peak around 7 km/h. Beyond that threshold, the contribution turns increasingly negative in a steady, steep decline: at the highest observed wind speeds (~55 km/h), the model multiplies predicted demand down by roughly a factor of e⁰·³⁴ ≈ 29% below the baseline. In short, calm winds are harmless, but strong winds progressively deter rentals.

[IMPORTANCE] Windspeed ranks 8th out of 9 features in global importance (score: 0.014), making it one of the least influential factors in the model. For comparison, the top feature — hour of the day — is roughly 60 times more important; even humidity and weather situation outrank wind speed considerably.

[RECOMMENDATION] Because wind speed only meaningfully suppresses demand at higher speeds (above ~20 km/h), operational teams could monitor wind forecasts and slightly reduce bike availability or maintenance staffing on notably windy days, while not over-reacting to mild or moderate breezes.
